A load of jobs\\\\nsubmitted together will fail together \\\\u2014 in time proximity, in the same region, sometimes\\\\nacross several queues at once \\\\u2014 while having unrelated causes.\\\\n\\\\nThis skill governs one specific, high-value correlation decision that the agent does not get\\\\nright on its own: **do not conflate incidents that belong to different job queues.**\\\\n\\\\n> Scope note. {"id": "7a98668e-7a6d-4402-9550-4ca32b67db87", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"text": "No — these should stay as two separate investigations.

I compared the `JobQueue` dimensions you gave: one alarm is scoped to `orders-queue`, the other to `billing-queue`. Those are different values, so per the correlation guardrail for Batch incidents, they must **not** be linked or treated as one incident, even though they're:

- In the same account and region
- Sharing overlapping compute environments
- Firing about a minute apart

Two Batch queues can share all of that infrastructure and still stall for entirely unrelated reasons (e.g., a bad job definition on one queue, a compute environment scaling limit on the other). The time proximity and shared compute environments are exactly the kind of surface-level correlation that leads to false conflation — shared infrastructure isn't a shared cause.

**Recommendation:** schedule these as two separate investigations, one primary on `orders-queue` and one on `billing-queue`. Want me to open investigations for both?", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}
